findings.topic: What RevenueCat Ads is (serving vs tracking)
findings.finding: "RevenueCat Ads" (docs name: "Ad Monetization") is a tracking/reporting layer over an existing ad SDK, NOT an ad server. Official docs: 'This integration works alongside your existing ad implementation—you're not replacing your ad SDK or changing how ads are served, just adding tracking to send ad events to RevenueCat.' It reports ad impressions, clicks, and revenue alongside subscription data.
findings.notes: Same statement repeated in the launch blog post and the 2026-03-25 changelog entry.

findings.topic: Is there a NEW ad-serving product in 2026?
findings.finding: No evidence of a new RevenueCat ad-serving/ad-network product as of 2026-07-31. The Shipaton 2026 phrase 'serve ads through RevenueCat Ads' (Devpost rules: 'uses the RevenueCat SDK to power at least one in-app or web purchase, or that serves ads through RevenueCat Ads') refers to the Ad Monetization beta (SDK ad tracking + AdMob convenience module + server-verified ad rewards). revenuecat.com/ads returns HTTP 404; the Shipaton announcement blog (2026-07-02) presents it as an existing option with no product launch, docs link, or waitlist; searches surfaced no ad-serving announcement.
findings.notes: Absence-of-evidence conclusion. The closest thing to 'serving' is the AdMob loadAndTrack convenience wrappers and rewarded-ad reward granting — ads still come from AdMob. A stealth/unannounced product can't be fully ruled out.

findings.finding: Direct convenience integration: Google AdMob only (iOS `RevenueCatAdMob` via `@_spi(Experimental) import RevenueCatAdMob`, Android `com.revenuecat.purchases.admob.*` with `@OptIn(ExperimentalPreviewRevenueCatPurchasesAPI::class)`; methods loadAndTrackBannerAd/InterstitialAd/RewardedAd/RewardedInterstitialAd/AppOpenAd, native via forNativeAdWithTracking). Manual integration supports any mediator exposing impression-level revenue data (ILRD): AppLovin MAX, ironSource (LevelPlay), Unity Ads, AdMob, and custom mediators. The Unity SDK ships MediatorName constants AdMob and AppLovin, with arbitrary custom strings allowed.
findings.notes: AdMob module details from https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/ad-monetization/admob (iOS purchases-ios 5.0+, Android purchases-android 8.0+; Unity/Flutter NOT supported by the convenience module).

findings.finding: Public beta, not GA. Changelog entry 'Track in-app ad revenue alongside your subscriptions' dated MAR 25, 2026 says 'now available in public beta'. Blog post (published 2026-04-13, updated 2026-04-16, by Francie Fernandes) states: 'Any customer can request access to the feature by navigating to the Ads page in their RevenueCat dashboard.' Ads Charts docs: 'This feature is currently in beta and requires access to be granted.' Ad revenue does not currently count toward Monthly Tracked Revenue (MTR). All SDK APIs are marked Experimental.
findings.notes: Blog: https://www.revenuecat.com/blog/growth/track-in-app-ad-revenue-alongside-purchases-get-the-full-picture-on-monetization. So: beta with dashboard opt-in/request-access, not a public waitlist page.

findings.topic: Unity SDK ad tracking support and version
findings.finding: Yes. purchases-unity 9.1.0, released 2026-05-27 (GitHub release note: 'feat: ad tracking API (#927) via Peter Porfy'), added `Purchases.AdTracker` (class RevenueCat.AdTracker) with TrackAdLoaded, TrackAdDisplayed, TrackAdOpened, TrackAdRevenue, TrackAdFailedToLoad, plus data classes AdLoadedData/AdDisplayedData/AdOpenedData/AdRevenueData/AdFailedToLoadData. PR #927 also touched PurchasesWrapper.java (Android) and PurchasesUnityHelper.m (iOS). Source is annotated 'Experimental: this API is unstable and may change in a future release.' Docs require purchases-unity 9.1.0+. Latest Unity release as of today: 9.7.0 (2026-07-31).
findings.notes: API surface verified directly from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RevenueCat/purchases-unity/main/RevenueCat/Scripts/AdTracker.cs and PR files https://api.github.com/repos/RevenueCat/purchases-unity/pulls/927/files. Enums: Format = banner, interstitial, rewarded, rewarded_interstitial, native, app_open, other; Precision = exact, publisher_defined, estimated, unknown; MediatorName = AdMob, AppLovin (+ custom string constructor).

findings.topic: Trackable ad events and dashboard metrics
findings.finding: Five event types: Loaded (ad successfully loads), Displayed (impression shown), Opened (user click/tap), Revenue (ILRD reported by mediation platform), Failed to Load. Dashboard Ads charts: Ad Impressions, Ad Clicks, Ad Revenue, Ad CTR, Ad eCPM, Ad Fill Rate, Ad Monetized Customers, Ad ARPDAU; segmentable by network, mediator, placement, ad unit, and format; data arrives via real-time SDK callbacks.
findings.notes: Event list corroborated by manual-integration docs and the AdTracker.cs Unity source (5 Track* methods map 1:1).

findings.topic: Per-platform minimum SDK versions for ad tracking
findings.finding: Ad tracking minimums per docs: purchases-android 8.0.0+, purchases-ios 5.0.0+ (iOS 15+), purchases_flutter 10.2.0+, purchases-unity 9.1.0+, react-native-purchases 10.2.0+. The separate 'Granting Ad Rewards' feature (server-verified rewarded-ad rewards granting virtual currency or timed entitlements, min 30 min) requires higher versions: purchases-ios 5.80.3+, purchases-android 10.12.0+, purchases_flutter 10.6.0+ (manual), react-native-purchases 10.5.0+ (manual) — Unity is NOT listed and no reward-verification APIs (generateRewardVerificationToken/pollRewardVerification) exist in purchases-unity main branch.
findings.notes: Versions extracted via WebFetch summarization of live docs — exact numbers are as reported by the page but worth a manual glance before publishing externally. Unity absence of reward APIs verified by grepping Purchases.cs/PurchasesWrapper.cs on main (only AdTracker methods present).

findings.topic: Catvertising award — technical qualification for a Unity Android game
findings.finding: Path: (1) Integrate purchases-unity >= 9.1.0 (latest 9.7.0); (2) request Ads beta access via the Ads page in the RevenueCat dashboard; (3) serve ads with an existing ad SDK/mediator in Unity (e.g., Google Mobile Ads Unity plugin, AppLovin MAX Unity, Unity LevelPlay) — the AdMob convenience module is native iOS/Android only, so Unity must use manual integration; (4) call Purchases.AdTracker.TrackAdLoaded/Displayed/Opened/FailedToLoad from ad SDK callbacks and TrackAdRevenue from the paid-event/ILRD callback (with MediatorName, Format, adUnitId, placement, revenue + Precision); (5) release the app in the submission window (rules: Jul 31 2026 8:00am PDT – Sep 30 2026 11:45pm PDT; app released Aug 1–Sep 30 per main page) and describe in the Devpost submission 'how the app uses RevenueCat Ads as a monetization method'. Judging: how natural/additive ads feel, fit with audience and broader revenue model. Prize: $15,000 first place.
findings.notes: Rules require the SDK to power at least one in-app/web purchase OR serve ads through RevenueCat Ads — ads alone qualify. Unity code shape (from docs): purchases.AdTracker.TrackAdLoaded(new AdLoadedData(mediatorName: AdTracker.MediatorName.AdMob, adFormat: AdTracker.Format.Rewarded, adUnitId: ad.adUnitId)). Rewarded-ad server verification is unavailable in Unity, so grant in-game rewards client-side or via your own backend.

findings.finding: The AdMob convenience module ('RevenueCatAdMob' on iOS, purchases-android admob artifact on Android) exists only for native iOS (purchases-ios 5.0+, iOS 15+) and Android (purchases-android 8.0+); Unity and Flutter are not mentioned/supported for it and must use manual AdTracker integration.
findings.notes: Beta banner present: 'This feature is currently in beta.'

revenuecat-ads.summary: "RevenueCat Ads" as referenced by Shipaton 2026 is RevenueCat's Ad Monetization feature — a public-beta tracking/reporting layer over an existing ad SDK, not an ad server: docs state explicitly that you keep your ad SDK and how ads are served is unchanged, and no 2026 ad-serving product announcement exists (revenuecat.com/ads is a 404); Devpost's "serve ads through RevenueCat Ads" is marketing shorthand. Launched in public beta via the 2026-03-25 changelog entry, access is requested from the Ads page in the dashboard (no public waitlist); all SDK APIs are marked Experimental and ad revenue doesn't count toward MTR. Integrations: an AdMob-only convenience module (native iOS/Android, loadAndTrack* methods) plus manual integration for any ILRD-capable mediator (AppLovin MAX, ironSource/LevelPlay, Unity Ads, AdMob, custom). The Unity SDK gained ad tracking in purchases-unity 9.1.0 (released 2026-05-27, "feat: ad tracking API (#927)") via Purchases.AdTracker with five methods — TrackAdLoaded, TrackAdDisplayed, TrackAdOpened, TrackAdRevenue, TrackAdFailedToLoad — matching the five trackable event types; latest Unity release is 9.7.0 (2026-07-31). A Unity Android game qualifies for Catvertising by integrating purchases-unity ≥9.1.0, getting Ads beta access, serving ads via its existing ad plugin (AdMob/MAX/LevelPlay Unity plugins), wiring AdTracker calls into ad callbacks (TrackAdRevenue from ILRD/paid events), releasing within the Jul 31–Sep 30 2026 window, and describing the ad strategy in the submission; note the AdMob convenience module and server-verified ad rewards are NOT available in Unity.
open_questions: Does RevenueCat plan to launch actual ad serving/mediation (making the Shipaton 'serve ads through RevenueCat Ads' wording literal) before or during Shipaton 2026? No announcement found as of 2026-07-31 — worth monitoring the changelog and App Growth Annual.
Will Unity get the Granting Ad Rewards verification APIs (generateRewardVerificationToken/pollRewardVerification) before Sep 30, 2026? Currently absent from purchases-unity main.

Exact per-platform minimum versions were extracted via summarized doc fetches (e.g., purchases-ios 5.0.0+ for tracking vs 5.80.3+ for rewards); a manual read of the live docs pages is advised before quoting them in published material.
Whether the beta access request from the dashboard Ads page is auto-approved or gated on review (docs say 'requires access to be granted' but approval latency is undocumented).

findings.finding: RevenueCat Test Store requires Unity SDK 8.3.0 minimum (iOS 5.43.0, Android 9.9.0, Flutter 9.8.0, RN 9.5.4, Capacitor 11.2.6, Cordova 7.2.0, KMP 2.2.2, Web JS 1.15.0). findings.finding: Consumables are supported (Android platform support row: 'Consumables, non-renewing subscriptions'; native Android SDK 7.11.0+ also supports non-consumable behavior). Coin-package offerings for games are the documented pattern. Key caveats: 'logic for keeping track of consumable redemptions must be handled outside of RevenueCat' — recommended to consume via server webhook NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE events; adding a consumable to an entitlement unlocks it forever after one purchase. When purchasing Android in-app products directly (not via Offerings), use PRODUCT_CATEGORY.NON_SUBSCRIPTION / PURCHASE_TYPE.INAPP in Unity.

Unity supports RestorePurchases with a documented C# sample (purchases.RestorePurchases((info, error) => ...)). Restores reactivate content bought on the same store account; cross-user restores follow the project's transfer behavior setting. Limitation: 'Consumables and non-renewing subscriptions can only be restored by using an account system with custom App User IDs' because they leave no receipt trace after being finished.

findings.topic: App Store promoted purchases in Unity
findings.finding: The Unity SDK exposes NO promoted-purchases API: GitHub code search over RevenueCat/purchases-unity returns 0 hits for 'promoted' and 'readyForPromoted', and Purchases.cs contains only PromotionalOffer (iOS promo discount) APIs — no deferment/ShouldPurchasePromoProduct handler. The RevenueCat docs index (llms.txt, 427 entries) contains no promoted-purchases page. Promoted purchases handling is a native purchases-ios delegate feature not bridged to Unity.
findings.notes: Absence verified by gh api code search + grep of main public API file; a bridge in another file is unlikely but not impossible.

findings.finding: Win-back offers are an Apple-only feature: RevenueCat's iOS Subscription Offers docs state 'Apple introduced win-back offers with iOS 18' and 'Win-Back Offers are only available to users on iOS18.0+'; redemption paths require purchases-ios 5.0.0–5.10.0+ (StoreKit message path 5.6.0+, paywall path 5.10.0+). There is NO Google Play win-back offer equivalent in RevenueCat docs — the Google Play Offers page covers only offers (free trial/intro) and promo codes. Separately, RevenueCat 'Win-back campaigns' (beta) are a WEB feature: churned mobile (App Store or Google Play) subscribers get an email with a Web Purchase Link — resubscription happens on web, not in Google Play.
findings.notes: Web win-back campaigns: https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/web/winback-campaigns (beta). Win-back offer APIs are not exposed in the Unity SDK either (no code hits).

findings.topic: Google Play promo codes for one-time products
findings.finding: Per RevenueCat's Google Play Offers docs: One-time codes (unique, auto-generated by Play Console, single-use) CAN be applied to in-app (one-time) products and can be redeemed in-app or in the Play Store app; Custom codes (developer-created, multi-redeem) can NOT be applied to in-app products (subscriptions only, in-app redemption only, limited to free-trial offers). 'Promo codes are limited by Google, on a per quarter basis' — exact quarterly quantities are deferred to Google's Play Console Help documentation.
findings.notes: Exact per-quarter caps not stated by RevenueCat; check support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer for current limits.

findings.finding: RevenueCat Virtual Currency is supported in Unity SDK 8.1.0+ (iOS 5.32.0+, Android 9.1.0+, RN 9.1.0+, Flutter 9.1.0+, Capacitor 11.1.0+, KMP 2.1.0+, Cordova 7.1.0+, Web 1.13.0+). Supports balance reads, server-side deposit/spend, and webhook transaction tracking.

RevenueCat Billing (Web Billing) is RevenueCat's own web billing engine: 'RevenueCat Billing uses Stripe as a payment gateway' (a connected Stripe account is required; only the project owner can connect it). It powers Web SDK, Web Purchase Links, Web Paywalls, Funnels, and Redemption Links (all listed ✅ Supported). Products/prices/trials/emails are configured in the RevenueCat dashboard. Limitation: cannot be used in India (no customer name/shipping address collection). Since 2026-04-17/2026-04-22, web purchase flows also support Stripe Billing products incl. Stripe Managed Payments (merchant-of-record); free trials through Stripe added 2026-05-29.
findings.notes: Stripe route changelog: https://www.revenuecat.com/release/sell-stripe-billing-products-in-web-purchase-flows-2026-04-17 and blog https://www.revenuecat.com/blog/company/stripe-managed-payments-revenuecat-web (2026-04-22).

findings.topic: Funnels + usability from a Unity Android game
findings.finding: RevenueCat Funnels are 'multi-step web experiences hosted by RevenueCat' (GA, included in the Pro plan at no additional cost). Payment providers: RevenueCat Billing, Stripe Billing (both need a connected Stripe account), or Paddle. Hosted on signup.cat or custom domains; Apple Pay/Google Pay auto-registered for Stripe-based configs. A Unity Android game CAN use them because purchases are web-side: entitlements reach the app via shared App User ID, or for anonymous traffic via Redemption Links ('required to use your funnels with anonymous users') redeemed in the mobile app; Web Purchase Link success pages 'can also be used to redirect the user back into the mobile app, using a custom URL scheme' and app_user_id is passed as a URL parameter. No mobile SDK version requirement — the funnel itself needs no SDK.
findings.notes: Also /docs/tools/funnels (GA + Pro plan) and /docs/web/web-billing/web-purchase-links.md. Caveat (inference, not from docs): steering Google Play users to external web checkout is governed by Google Play's payments policy — see RevenueCat's app-to-web guidelines blog https://www.revenuecat.com/blog/engineering/app-to-web-purchase-guidelines.

findings.finding: RevenueCat Shipaton 2026 (Devpost) runs Aug 1 – Sep 30, 2026 (deadline Sep 30 11:45pm PDT), $685,000+ total prizes. The 'Funnel Vision Award — Stripe' ($15,000 / $10,000 / $5,000 for 1st–3rd) 'Recognizes a project that launches a web funnel using RevenueCat Funnels and Stripe', judged on qualifying web payment volume processed during the measurement period plus design/functionality/implementation. findings.finding: Webhooks send POST JSON for purchase lifecycle events (and optionally Paywall UI events: impressions, closes, etc. — these lack transaction fields). Config: HTTPS URL, optional authorization header, env filter (production/sandbox), per-app or project-wide, event-type filtering. Server must return 200 within 60s; failures retried up to 5 times with 5/10/20/40/80-minute delays. Delivery is at-least-once (dedupe on event id recommended); most events arrive in 5–60s, cancellations within ~2h. Consumable flow: NON_RENEWING_PURCHASE events recommended for granting coins/gems server-side.
findings.notes: Event catalog: https://www.revenuecat.com/docs/integrations/webhooks/event-types-and-fields

findings.finding: OneSignal-Unity-SDK latest release is 5.3.2, published 2026-07-23. It wraps OneSignal Android native SDK 5.9.7 and iOS native SDK 5.5.5. Preceding releases: 5.3.1 (2026-07-14), 5.3.0 (2026-07-10, added OneSignal project settings + location opt-out), 5.2.11 (2026-06-24), 5.2.8 (2026-05-19, fixed Unity custom-event nested property encoding). A rel/5.3.3 branch and an unreleased v6 branch exist in the repo.
findings.notes: Verified via GitHub API (api.github.com/repos/OneSignal/OneSignal-Unity-SDK/releases), not search snippets.

findings.finding: Unity SDK requires Unity 2022.3 or newer; install via Unity Asset Store or UPM scoped registry (npmjs). Android: enable Custom Main Gradle Template and Custom Gradle Properties Template, target API level 33 or higher, run External Dependency Manager > Android Resolver > Force Resolve; if minification is enabled copy the Android plugin to assets. iOS: iOS 12+/iPadOS 12+ (simulator iOS 16.2+); SDK auto-configures Xcode settings. Init: OneSignal.Initialize("YOUR_APP_ID") in a MonoBehaviour Start().

Journey step types (exact names): Wait (minutes/hours/days/weeks), Wait Until (conditions: segment entry, message events delivered/opened/clicked, or custom events; supports multiple conditions with branching on first met; requires expiration; only one message event per Wait Until step), Time Window (restrict to specific days/times, release randomized within 15 min), Yes/No Branch (segment membership or push/email message behavior), Split Branch (random split across up to 20 branches, equal or custom %, nestable for A/B/N + control), Tag User (add/remove tags), message steps (push, email, SMS, in-app), and webhook steps (HTTP with Liquid personalization, retries). Once live, Yes/No and Split branches cannot be restructured.

Entry rules are either Segment-based (Include/Exclude Segment) or Custom Event-based (with optional 'Filter by property' conditions) — 'Entry rules cannot combine Segments and Custom Events. You must choose one type per Journey.' No API-based entry rule documented. Exit rules: user becomes active (new SDK session), custom event condition, no longer matches audience, enters a segment; optional tag apply/remove on early exit. Re-entry timer starts at exit; custom-event Journeys always allow re-entry, segment-based have configurable windows. Goals feature is Beta.

Journeys exist on all plans but the number of active Journeys is plan-limited: Free = 1 active journey with 2 message steps; Growth = 3 active journeys with 6 message steps; Professional = 20 active journeys with 50 message steps; Enterprise = unlimited/custom. Docs say 'The number of active Journeys depends on your plan.'
findings.notes: Journey numbers agreed across two independent fetches of the pricing page plus journeys-overview doc.

findings.finding: Custom events ARE available in the Unity SDK: introduced in Unity SDK 5.2.0 (published 2026-01-30; beta 5.2.0-beta-01 on 2025-10-08). Method: OneSignal.User.TrackEvent("name") or TrackEvent(name, Dictionary<string, object> properties) with nested dictionaries supported (nested-property encoding bug fixed in 5.2.8, 2026-05-19). The mobile SDK reference lists trackEvent for Kotlin, Java, Swift, Obj-C, Unity C#, React Native, Flutter, Cordova/Ionic; a REST 'Create Custom Events API' also exists.
findings.notes: Also confirmed at https://documentation.onesignal.com/docs/en/mobile-sdk-reference#trackevent with Unity C# code example. The 5.2.0 release note said to contact support@onesignal.com to enable the feature per app (early rollout, Jan 2026).

findings.topic: Custom events — plan gating and limits
findings.finding: Docs state verbatim: 'Custom Events are available on all paid plans.' Limits: event name max 128 characters, max event payload 2024 bytes, max request size (multiple events) 1 MB. Custom events can start a Journey, gate Wait Until steps, act as exit rules, and personalize messages. Custom Event segmentation is in Early Access (request via support@onesignal.com).
findings.notes: CONFLICT: one fetch of onesignal.com/pricing rendered the Custom Events row as '—' for all tiers; the docs quote is explicit, so treat 'all paid plans' as authoritative but verify the exact tier in the dashboard.

findings.finding: Unity tag methods: OneSignal.User.AddTag(key, value), AddTags, RemoveTag(s), GetTags() returning Dictionary<string,string>. Pricing page limits 'data tags': Free = 2, Growth = 10, Professional = 100, Enterprise = custom. Segments: Free = 6, Growth = 10, Professional = 20, Enterprise = custom.
findings.notes: Method names High confidence; tag/segment count rows from a single pricing-page fetch (Medium).

findings.finding: IAM is fully supported in the Unity SDK (mobile-only channel; no web IAM). Unity C# trigger API: OneSignal.InAppMessages.AddTrigger(key,value), AddTriggers, RemoveTrigger(s), ClearTriggers. Journey in-app steps only display on a new session (app reopened after 30+ s background). Pricing: Free = 1 active in-app message; Growth = 'Unlimited, included with mobile push'.

Recommended pattern: an in-app message with the 'Push Permission Prompt' click action (soft prompt) — 'Dismissing a soft prompt does not consume a system prompt attempt.' iOS gives 1 system prompt attempt, Android 13+ gives 2; Android 12 and earlier auto-grants permission at install; Android 13 (API 33) added runtime permission. If attempts are exhausted the click action routes to app notification settings. SDK methods: requestPermission(fallbackToSettings: true) and optIn() (optIn also clears opt-out state). iOS provisional delivery via Settings > Apple iOS > 'Enable iOS 12 direct to history'. Timing guidance: prompt after a value moment, not first launch.

Push frequency capping 'limits how many push notifications a single user can receive in a rolling minute, hour, day, or week window'; applies to push only ('does not apply to email, SMS, or in-app messages'); configured at Settings > Push & In-app > Frequency Capping. Docs: 'available on select paid plans'; the pricing table shows it available only on Enterprise ('—' for Free/Growth/Professional).
findings.notes: 'Enterprise only' from two pricing-page fetches that agreed; docs deliberately vague ('select paid plans').

findings.finding: OneSignal has NO per-user push 'quiet hours' feature. Grep of the full docs corpus (llms-full.txt) shows 'quiet hours' only in SMS regulatory-compliance context ('Promotional messages must respect local quiet hours. Use Journey time windows to ensure messages send within permitted hours.'). The supported mechanisms for time-of-day control are the Journey 'Time Window' step, scheduled/timezone-based delivery on individual sends, and push throttling (with a 24-hour delivery-completion rule).
findings.notes: Third-party marketing pages claim OneSignal has 'quiet hours' — not supported by official docs for push.

findings.finding: Options: verified App Links (https:// URLs, requires android:autoVerify="true" intent filter + assetlinks.json at /.well-known/) and custom URI schemes (myapp://, registered in AndroidManifest; fail silently if app not installed; don't work in email/SMS). On Android 12+ a non-verified https:// link opens the browser, not the app. Recommended mobile pattern: put a deep_link key in Additional Data and route in a OneSignal.Notifications click listener (event.notification.additionalData / launchURL) — works identically in Unity C#. No Unity/game-specific deep-link doc exists.

Unity SDK identity: OneSignal.Login(external_id) links device to a known user; Logout() unlinks; plus AddAlias(es)/RemoveAlias(es), getOnesignalId/getExternalId. RevenueCat integration (for OneSignal SDK v5+): call OneSignal login first, then send the OneSignal ID to RevenueCat as subscriber attribute $onesignalUserId (helper setOnesignalUserID()); RevenueCat 'validates the associated externalId'. Legacy v4-and-below uses $onesignalId (player ID) via setOnesignalID(). RevenueCat then writes subscription-lifecycle tags onto the OneSignal user: app_user_id, period_type, purchased_at, expiration_at, store, environment, last_event_type, product_id, entitlement_ids, active_subscription, subscription_status, grace_period_expiration_at. Events synced as tags include initial purchase, trial started/converted/cancelled, renewal, cancellation, uncancellation, expiration, billing issue, product change.
findings.notes: Cross-checked against https://documentation.onesignal.com/docs/en/revenuecat.md — both agree on the tag list and v5 flow (integration syncs tags, not custom events).

findings.finding: Outcomes are still supported and documented (not renamed; docs page is 'Custom Outcomes'). Unity C# methods: OneSignal.Session.AddOutcome("NAME"), AddUniqueOutcome("NAME"), AddOutcomeWithValue("NAME", 3.14). Outcomes track actions/revenue attributed to push and in-app messages; IAM click actions can also record outcomes.
findings.notes: Also https://documentation.onesignal.com/docs/en/custom-outcomes.md

findings.finding: Channels (called 'Android Notification Categories' by OneSignal) can be created in the dashboard (Settings > Push & In-App > Android Notification Channels) or programmatically in app code. Importance options: Low (silent), Medium (no sound/vibration), High (sound/vibrate, no pop-up), Urgent (sound + heads-up). Custom sounds and vibration patterns (ms values, e.g. 0,300,500,300) supported. Target via API with android_channel_id (dashboard-created) or existing_android_channel_id (code-created). OneSignal auto-creates two default categories; channels are an Android 8.0+ concept.

Android push requires uploading a Firebase Cloud Messaging Service Account private key JSON to the OneSignal dashboard; the service account needs cloudmessaging.messages.create and firebase.projects.get permissions. 'Google legacy FCM APIs are now fully deprecated' — legacy server keys (AIz...) must be migrated to FCM v1. The FCM credentials doc does not require google-services.json for the OneSignal Unity flow (the Unity setup doc handles Android config via gradle templates + EDM4U).

Four plans: Free ($0): 10,000 free email sends/mo, unlimited mobile push, web push max 10,000 subscribers per send, 1 active journey (2 message steps), 1 active in-app message, 6 segments, 2 data tags. Growth (starts $19/mo): mobile push $0.012 per MAU, web push $0.004 per subscriber, 20,000 free email sends then $1.50/1,000, 3 journeys (6 steps), unlimited IAM with mobile push, 10 segments, 10 data tags. Professional (custom, annual): 20 journeys (50 steps), 20 segments, 100 data tags, SMS/RCS available. Enterprise (custom, annual): unlimited journeys/steps, frequency capping, custom segments/tags, dedicated CSM/SLA.
findings.notes: Two fetches agreed on journeys, IAM, email, and price figures; they disagreed on the Custom Events row (one said absent from Free/Growth, one said '—' everywhere) while docs say custom events are on all paid plans. Pricing page is JS-heavy; exact rows warrant a human eyeball.

findings.topic: Known issue — Android 16 KB page size
findings.finding: GitHub issue #789 ('Related with android page size 16kb', opened 2025-05-22, closed 2025-06-11): OneSignal staff (nan-li) stated the OneSignal SDK is compliant with the 16 KB page-size requirement because it uses only Java/Kotlin code (no native .so libraries), citing developer.android.com/guide/practices/page-sizes#16-kb-impact. No open 16 KB issues in the Unity SDK repo.

Google Play requires new apps and app updates to target Android 16 (API level 36) by August 31, 2026 (extension available to November 1, 2026); existing apps must target at least API 35 by the same date to remain discoverable to new users. OneSignal's Unity setup doc only mandates target API 33+, so targeting 36 satisfies it; no API-36-specific issues found in the Unity SDK repo (GitHub search returned only unrelated old issues).

Current OneSignal Unity 5.x still uses Google's EDM4U (setup doc: Assets > External Dependency Manager > Android Resolver > Force Resolve). PR #892 'fix: [SDK-4927] migrate to Unity External Dependency Manager' was merged 2026-07-23 into the unreleased v6 branch because 'Unity Asset Store rejected the v6 submission because it referenced Google's superseded EDM4U package. Unity now requires package maintainers to use com.unity.external-dependency-manager' (2.0). Unity's EDM 2.0 docs state 'It's recommended to have only one external dependency manager installed at a time' and treat Google's EDM4U as a competing alternative — so mixing OneSignal 5.x (Google EDM4U) with plugins that adopt Unity EDM 2.0 is the active conflict surface. Historical EDM4U-era conflicts exist (e.g. issue #862 'Duplicate class androidx.activity.ComponentActivity', closed 2026-03-26; older AdMob AndroidX conflicts #192). GitHub search found ZERO RevenueCat-conflict issues in the OneSignal Unity repo. Latest neighboring plugins: Google Mobile Ads Unity v11.3.0 (2026-07-19), RevenueCat purchases-unity 9.7.0 (2026-07-31).
findings.notes: Unity EDM 2.0 manual: https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.external-dependency-manager@2.0/manual/get-started-with-edm.html. Whether GMA/RevenueCat Unity plugins have themselves migrated to Unity EDM 2.0 was NOT verified.

findings.finding: A dedicated 'Event-driven Journeys' guide exists covering Custom Events as entry rules, Wait Until conditions, exit rules, and message personalization sources; supporting integration docs (BigQuery, Kafka, Pub/Sub, etc.) sync server-side custom events into Journeys.
findings.notes: URL confirmed present in the official docs index (llms.txt); page body not separately fetched.

onesignal-unity-sdk.summary: OneSignal Unity SDK is current at 5.3.2 (released 2026-07-23, wrapping Android native 5.9.7 / iOS 5.5.5); it requires Unity 2022.3+, Android target API 33+, gradle template customization, and Google's EDM4U — while an unreleased v6 branch (PR #892, merged 2026-07-23) migrates to Unity's official com.unity.external-dependency-manager 2.0 after the Asset Store rejected the Google EDM4U dependency, making dual-dependency-manager coexistence the main current conflict risk (no RevenueCat-specific conflict issues exist; the 16 KB page-size question was closed 2025-06-11 as "compliant — Java/Kotlin only"). Custom events shipped in the Unity SDK in 5.2.0 (2026-01-30) as OneSignal.User.TrackEvent with nested-property support, are usable as Journey entry rules, Wait Until conditions, and exit rules, and are "available on all paid plans" (not Free). Journeys support Wait, Wait Until, Time Window, Yes/No Branch, Split Branch (up to 20), Tag User, webhook, and push/email/SMS/in-app message steps, with plan limits of 1/3/20/unlimited active journeys on Free/Growth($19+/mo)/Professional/Enterprise. There is no push "quiet hours" feature (Time Window steps are the substitute), and frequency capping is push-only and effectively Enterprise-gated. Tags, in-app triggers, Login(external_id) aliasing (RevenueCat consumes it via $onesignalUserId and writes subscription tags back), outcomes (OneSignal.Session.AddOutcome, still supported under "Custom Outcomes"), and dashboard/code Android notification channels are all fully available from Unity; Android push needs an FCM v1 Service Account JSON uploaded to OneSignal. Google Play's API 36 deadline is 2026-08-31 for new apps/updates, comfortably above OneSignal's API-33 minimum.

findings.topic: 8a. Google Play fee tiers — MAJOR CHANGE effective 2026-06-30 (US/UK/EEA)
findings.finding: Official Google sources confirm: legacy structure (still applies outside US/UK/EEA) = 15% on first $1M USD/year, 30% above $1M, 15% flat on auto-renewing subscriptions. NEW structure effective June 30, 2026 in US, UK, EEA (post-Epic settlement): service fee decoupled from billing — 10% service fee on first $1M and on all auto-renewing subscriptions; one-time purchases: 'new installs' (first install/update on/after regional launch date) lower rate vs 'existing installs' higher rate (reported by 9to5Google/press as 20% vs 25% totals); +5% billing fee only if using Google Play's billing; alternative billing/external payment links now allowed with no billing fee. Google states 99% of fee-paying developers were eligible for <=15%.
findings.notes: Primary: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/112622 (live fee page) and https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/16954621 (lower-fees page). Exact new/existing-install percentages render as rate-card images on the official blog; the 20%/25% totals come from press (https://9to5google.com/2026/06/24/google-play-store-external-billing-june-30/) — verify rate card manually before quoting in anything contractual. For an indie under $1M in the US the effective take is now 10% + 5% = 15% via Play billing, or 10% with own billing.

benchmarks-econ.summary: Verified 2025-2026 benchmarks where they exist and flagged stale/fabricated ones. eCPM: the only text-verifiable measured figures are Tenjin+CAS.AI Q2 2024 (US Android rewarded $30.25, interstitial $16.15, banner $1.18) and Appodeal Q4 2024 (US rewarded $15.15 blended, NA Android rewarded $9.20, interstitial $9.70, banner $0.55) — Tenjin's 2026 report contains Q1 2025-Q1 2026 data but locks all numbers in chart images, so treat US Android rewarded as a $15-30 range pending manual chart extraction. Retention: the puzzle-specific 31.85/12.18/5.35 figures every 2026 article quotes are actually AppsFlyer Q3 2022 data (OUTDATED); the current measured picture is GameAnalytics 2026 (2025 data, 16.2k games): median D1 ~22% / D7 ~4% / D30 ~0.7%, top-10% ~40/12/4, with puzzle/board/card qualitatively the best long-retention genres, and Adjust putting all-genre D1 at 27%. CPI: Adjust 2026 measured global gaming CPI $0.56 (+30% YoY), North America $1.68; puzzle-specific iOS $3/Android $2 is secondhand 2024-vintage Business of Apps data. IAP conversion: AppsFlyer 2026 gives casino 4.95% pay-within-30-days and casual D90 IAP ARPU $1.34/ARPPU $7.26, but the exact casual conversion % is gated. Critically for the caller: Google Play's fee structure changed on June 30, 2026 for US/UK/EEA — 10% service fee (first $1M and all subscriptions) + 5% billing fee only when using Play billing, external billing now allowed — so the old flat "15% first $1M" framing is outdated for US users. No credible public benchmarks exist for puzzle ARPDAU, puzzle rewarded opt-in % of DAU, Google Play refund norms, or puzzle-category store CVR; report those as gaps rather than citing blog numbers.

market-competitors.summary: Direct whitespace confirmed: as of 31 Jul 2026, four Google Play searches (cat train / cat metro / cat subway / kitty train) surface no cat-themed metro or route-switching puzzle — nearest neighbors are idle cat-train tycoons (Cat Train Tycoon 547K installs, Animal Express 314K), while the mechanical ancestors are absent (Trainyard delisted since 2019, Mini Motorways never shipped on Android, STATIONflow/Overcrowd PC-only). The genre's poles are sharply drawn in the store data: premium transit puzzles are beloved but small (Mini Metro $0.99, 3.6M installs, 4.63, praised for visuals/no-ads but criticized for endgame micromanagement; Railbound $4.99, 211K installs despite an Apple Design Award and OpenCritic 83), while 2025-26 one-thumb routing F2P hits are enormous but hated for monetization (Arrows 103.6M installs in 12 months with 'ad every other level' complaints; Bus Traffic Fever 15.4M installs in 5 months but only 3.72 stars on forced-30s-ad and level-recycling complaints). Cat theming demonstrably carries 10M+ installs on charm alone across three distinct monetization intensities: Neko Atsume (13.6M, 4.78, IAP capped at $3.49), Cat Snack Bar (29.8M, IAP to $99.99), Cats & Soup (42.7M, 4.65, IAP to $84.99, cosmetics-driven). Premium-vs-F2P math on same-day store counters shows a 25-500x install gap, and Cat Museum's quiet conversion from $2.99 premium to free+IAP underlines it; the Meowdoku clone swarm (7+ lookalikes within ~3 months) warns that any cat-puzzle hit gets fast-followed immediately. The strategic opening the data supports: a cat-commuter routing puzzle with Mini Metro-grade polish, Neko Atsume-grade gentle monetization (or premium unlock), and explicit no-forced-ads positioning attacks the single loudest complaint in every F2P competitor's reviews.

findings.topic: Grand Prize winner Payout — verified traction
findings.finding: Payout (class-action settlement discovery app, solo dev Connor Burd) won the 2025 Grand Prize 'Build & Grow Award' ($65,000) with 17,000+ users, $30,017 revenue, 1,750+ paying subscribers, and 500,000+ X (Twitter) impressions during the competition window. Built 100% with AI tools (Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT; 'not one line of code written by hand'), React Native + Node.js/TypeScript on Vercel, initial build in 10 days, shipped to both App Store and Play Store.
findings.notes: The 500K figure is social impressions, NOT downloads — a search snippet claiming '500,000+ downloads' conflicts with both primary sources and should be treated as unverified. Payout's Devpost story credits 'capturing high value keywords' (ASO) as high-leverage growth; no paid-ads channel is claimed.

findings.finding: No dedicated Best Game award existed in 2025. Game/game-adjacent winners: (1) Crystal Abyss — sole Staff & Sponsors Award winner — a Columns-style falling-gem puzzle themed on Dante's nine circles of hell, SpriteKit+SwiftUI, fully AI-assisted coding; (2) Otter Day: Weekday Guesser — Best Vibes 1st ($15k) — a learning game for calculating the weekday of any date, solo-built with Perplexity Pro, KlingAI, ElevenLabs; (3) DrawIt: A Multiplatform Draw & Guess Game — Kotlin Multiplatform 4th ($5k) — multiplayer sketch/guess with leaderboards, KMP across iOS/Android/desktop + Firebase; (4) Vector Guard — HAMM (monetization) 1st ($15k) — gamified (not a game) insect-identification app using CDC data, won on its creative '1:50 Justice Model' monetization.
findings.notes: Pattern: the games that won took non-game categories (vibes, platform reach, staff pick, monetization). All were small, single-mechanic, heavily AI-assisted builds — none won on scale/traction.

findings.finding: 2025 Grand Prize criterion (verbatim, Devpost): 'the app that releases early and iterates to grow their app the fastest. Judges want to hear about what you've done post-release to push your app growth to the next level.' 2026 official rules add: Grand Prize shortlist is created by comparing 'total revenue generated by eligible Projects during the Submission Period, as reported in RevenueCat', and 'Judges may consider the quality, efficiency, and sustainability of the growth that produced the revenue, rather than revenue alone'; entrants must document post-launch product improvements, user-acquisition/retention efforts, and marketing experiments 'linked to concrete results'.
findings.notes: Revenue-in-RevenueCat is the objective gate for the Grand Prize; the narrative of growth efforts is the tiebreaker. Category awards (Design, Vibes, Peace, HAMM) are judged on craft/story, not traction.

findings.topic: Official 'How to win Shipaton' blog series (organizer guidance)
findings.finding: Four-part series by Perttu Lähteenlahti (45 wins in 70+ hackathons): Part 1 (2025-08-04) — build a 'Minimum Lovable Product': 'identify the absolute smallest surface area that communicates your product's value — and then making sure that piece feels magical'; solve a real multi-person problem, start narrow. Part 2 — build fast with the '4-8-24 method', relentless beta testing, AI use, continuous polish. Part 3 (2025-08-22) — target '100 paying customers during Shipaton'; growth advice is entirely organic: existing networks, niche Reddit/Discord communities, micro-influencers ('small-scale influencers can often drive more adoption than a big account'), ASO ('can have a huge impact'), Shipaton community cross-promo; paid ads are never recommended. Part 4 (2025-09-05) — pitch via Dan Harmon's Story Circle; 'judges and users don't care that your app has a chart, they care that it helps someone feel progress'; include metrics like 'retention, completion, time saved' and traction signals; hook in the first 15–20 seconds of the video.
findings.notes: Part 2 verified via search result summary only (not direct fetch) — content direction confirmed but quote wording there is Medium confidence.

findings.topic: Marketing / paid acquisition influence on judging
findings.finding: Neither the 2025 nor 2026 official rules restrict paid user acquisition, but no winner is documented as winning via paid ads. Marketing explicitly IS judged: 2025 Buzziest Launch award (verbatim: 'teams that make the biggest splash during their launch (e.g., viral social campaigns, creative marketing stunts)') went to ReadHim ($1,100 MRR in 10 days; 5.2M Instagram views). 2026 rules temper pure spend: judges 'may consider the quality, efficiency, and sustainability of the growth that produced the revenue, rather than revenue alone.' Winning growth stories were organic: Payout 500K X impressions + ASO keywords; Gurwi (#BuildInPublic 1st) 13,000+ users, 1,000+ reviews, 4.9 rating via building in public.
findings.notes: Absence of paid-acquisition restrictions confirmed from rules text; absence of paid-ads-driven winners is inference from winner writeups (no winner disclosed ad spend). The 'sustainability of growth' clause suggests judges would discount bought installs.

shipaton-winners-meta.summary: Shipaton's Grand Prize is won on measurable post-launch growth, verified in RevenueCat's own revenue data: 2025 winner Payout (solo dev, 100% AI-written via Claude Code/Cursor, shipped in 10 days) posted 17,000+ users, $30,017 revenue, 1,750+ paying subscribers, and 500K X impressions, grown via ASO keywords and organic social, not paid ads. The 2026 rules make the mechanism explicit — a revenue-ranked shortlist from RevenueCat data, with judges weighing "quality, efficiency, and sustainability of the growth… rather than revenue alone" — and no rule restricts paid acquisition, though no 2025 winner is documented as buying installs. 2025 had 812 submissions from 51,886 registrants ($355k+ pool); category awards were winnable at far lower traction (1k–13k users, $1k–2k revenue) on craft and story. findings.topic: 5. Data Safety form - general SDK responsibility
findings.finding: Developers must declare all user data transmitted off-device including via third-party SDKs: "This includes data collected and handled through any third-party libraries or SDKs used in their apps" and "You alone are responsible for making complete and accurate declarations." Inaccurate declarations can lead to enforcement (rejection, removal, blocked updates). Requirement fully in force since July 20, 2022.
findings.source_date: Page shows last updated March 31, 2023 (per fetched content)

findings.topic: 5a. Data Safety - AdMob (Google Mobile Ads SDK)
findings.finding: Google's official disclosure page: the SDK automatically collects IP address (approx location), user product interactions (app launch, taps, video views), diagnostics (launch time, hang rate, energy usage), and device/account identifiers (Android advertising ID, app set ID), for advertising, analytics, and fraud prevention; all encrypted in transit (TLS). Developers can disable ad ID collection via manifest.
findings.notes: Declare these as Collected and Shared (advertising) in the Data safety form.

findings.finding: OneSignal docs: by default the SDK collects in-app purchases and app interactions (session counts, durations, notification clicks); select at minimum the purposes "Analytics" and "Developer communications" for App interactions; GAID is NOT collected by default; emails/phone numbers/Tags must be declared additionally if used; app interactions marked processed ephemerally.

RevenueCat docs: declare "Purchase history" (Financial info) as Collected; purposes "App functionality" and "Analytics"; ephemeral = No; collection required (cannot be turned off); data encrypted in transit; deletion available via RevenueCat dashboard/REST API. Personal info and device identifiers only if you use customer attributes or ad-ID integrations (gpsAdId/androidId). "Shared" only if using third-party integrations that are not service providers.
findings.notes: Any additional analytics SDK must be declared per the same rules.

findings.finding: Full-screen interstitials of all formats that show unexpectedly (e.g., during gameplay, at level start, before splash screen) are prohibited; interstitials must be closeable after 15 seconds (opted-in/non-disruptive ones may persist longer); ads must not force clicks or block core use and must be easily dismissible without penalty. Explicit exemption: "This policy does not apply to rewarded ads which are explicitly opted-in by users." Also: "The ads and their associated offers ... shown within your app must be appropriate for the content rating of your app" (teen-rated app requires teen-appropriate ads).

findings.topic: 6b. Families policy triggers / cute cat art style
findings.finding: Families obligations are triggered by the developer's own Target audience and content declaration in Play Console (age groups from "Ages 5 and under" to "18 and over"): if at least one selected age group includes children, the full Families Policy applies, including using only Families Self-Certified Ads SDKs for ads served to children/unknown-age users. A cute art style does NOT automatically force child-directed treatment, but the page states: "If your app is not primarily designed for children under 13 but your listing contains marketing elements that suggest otherwise (such as youthful animation or young characters in the graphic assets), Google Play may reject your app" - remedies are removing those store-listing elements or reclassifying target age groups.
findings.notes: Quotes are from the fetched page; the fetch also claimed a "minors under 21 in applicable jurisdictions" scenario which looks paraphrased/unreliable and is excluded. Practical takeaway: declare 13+ only, keep store listing art/copy from reading as child-directed, or accept Families obligations.

findings.finding: Google Play enforces a time-bound quota on how often a user can see the review dialog; calling launchReviewFlow more than once in a short period ("for example, less than a month") may not display the dialog. Explicit note: "The specific value of the quota is an implementation detail, and it can be changed by Google Play without any notice." Guidance: don't prompt excessively, trigger only after sufficient app experience, and do NOT put a call-to-action button that triggers the API (redirect to the Play Store listing for user-initiated rating instead).
findings.notes: No exact numeric quota is published; do not rely on any specific number.

findings.finding: Applies ONLY if the app allows users to create an account from within the app ("a unique user identity ... user-facing feature", typically username/email/password). If so, required: (1) an in-app path to delete the account and associated data, (2) a web link resource for deletion requests (entered in the Data safety form), (3) completed data-deletion questions in the Data safety form. In force since Dec 7, 2023 (extension window ended May 31, 2024); non-compliance can lead to removal.
findings.notes: A game using only RevenueCat anonymous app user IDs with no user-facing account creation does not trigger this; adding sign-in (e.g., Play Games profile is exempt as Google's own, but custom accounts are not) does.

findings.topic: 9. App content declarations at first release
findings.finding: Per "Prepare your app for review": required for all apps - privacy policy link (store listing and in-app, mandatory for apps requesting sensitive permissions or targeting children; in practice Play Console requires a privacy policy URL for all new apps), ads declaration ("You must declare whether or not your app contains ads"), target audience and content (target age group), content rating questionnaire (IARC; unrated apps may be removed - ratings generated per authority: ESRB, PEGI, USK, ACB, ClassInd, GRAC, generic IARC). Conditional: app access/sign-in details (if any part is login-gated), permissions declaration form (high-risk/sensitive permissions), news apps, COVID-19 apps. Data safety form (answer/10787469) and account-deletion questions (answer/13327111) are additionally mandatory. Financial features and health declarations exist in Play Console App content but were not itemized on this page.
findings.notes: For a paid-IAP game: expect Financial features = "no financial features" and Health = none; exact current Play Console item list (incl. EU trader status/DSA declaration) requires checking inside Play Console - flagged as open question.

findings.topic: 10. Store review duration for first release
findings.finding: Google: "For certain developer accounts, we'll take more time to thoroughly review your app to help better protect users. This may result in review times of up to seven days or longer in exceptional cases." Same up-to-7-days-or-longer wording applies to apps subject to extended reviews. Managed publishing lets you control the go-live moment after approval. For a NEW personal account, total time-to-production = closed test (>=14 days with 12 opted-in testers) + production-access review (usually <=7 days) + first-release review (up to 7 days or longer).
findings.notes: Plan 4-6 weeks of buffer before a hard Aug-Sep 2026 launch date given the closed-testing gate on new personal accounts.

google-play-policy.summary: All ten areas were verified against official pages fetched 2026-07-31. Hard deadlines stacking on an Aug-Sep 2026 launch: target API 36 (Android 16) required for new apps/updates from Aug 31, 2026 (extension to Nov 1, 2026 via Play Console Policy status page); Billing Library 8+ required from the same date (BL7 is the minimum today; extension also Nov 1, 2026); and 16 KB page-size support has been mandatory since Nov 1, 2025 for anything targeting API 35+, so it is unavoidable at API 36. RevenueCat's current Android SDK is compliant: latest release 10.16.0 (2026-07-31) pins com.android.billingclient:billing 8.3.0, with BC8 adopted since 9.0.0 (2025-07-10). For a personal account created after Nov 13, 2023, the closed-testing gate is currently 12 testers opted in continuously for the last 14 days, then an "Apply for production" questionnaire reviewed usually in <=7 days, then a first-release review of up to 7 days or longer - so total time-to-store is realistically 3-5+ weeks. Ads rules: no unexpected full-screen interstitials (none at level start/before splash), interstitials closeable within 15 s, opted-in rewarded ads exempt, and ad content must match the app's content rating; a cute cat art style does not automatically force child-directed treatment, but child-suggestive store-listing elements can trigger rejection or forced reclassification, and declaring any under-13 age group activates full Families policy including Families Self-Certified Ads SDKs. Data safety declarations must cover SDK-collected data: AdMob (IP, interactions, diagnostics, ad ID/app set ID; advertising/analytics/fraud prevention), OneSignal (app interactions; Analytics + Developer communications), RevenueCat (purchase history; App functionality + Analytics). Account deletion obligations apply only if the app itself offers account creation; the in-app review API has an unpublished, changeable quota and must not be wired to a visible button.
